children: Vistagen reported preliminary positive OLE data showing fasedienol was well-tolerated and associated with clinically relevant improvement in social anxiety over four months.
OLE safety population N=322: fasedienol 3.2 µg as-needed up to six times/day for up to 12 months was well-tolerated.
Discontinuations due to adverse events 1.6% (5/322); no discontinuations attributed to fasedienol and no drug-related serious AEs.
Most TEAEs mild/moderate; common events: headache 18.0%, URTI 9.9%, rhinorrhoea 7.1%, oropharyngeal pain 5.3%.
LSAS mean change from baseline improved over months 1–4: 20.2, 24.6, 29.1, 31.4 points respectively; ≥20-point responders rose to 65% at Month 4.
SPIN mean improvement increased from 10.5 points at Month 1 to 14.9 points at Month 4; 59% had ≥10-point improvement at Month 4.

title: Vistagen reports positive open-label extension safety and exploratory efficacy for fasedienol in social anxiety
